claim: DNS Firewall filters and regulates outbound DNS traffic for VPCs; a Firewall Manager DNS Firewall policy associates each DNS Firewall rule group in the policy with each in-scope VPC in every in-scope account.
question: What does a Firewall Manager DNS Firewall policy create in member accounts?

values.display: filtering and regulation of outbound DNS traffic for your VPCs
creates an association between each DNS Firewall rule group

evidence.quote: DNS Firewall provides filtering and regulation of outbound DNS traffic for your VPCs. You create reusable collections of filtering rules in DNS Firewall rule groups and you associate the rule groups to your VPCs. When you apply the Firewall Manager policy, for each account and VPC that's within policy scope, Firewall Manager creates an association between each DNS Firewall rule group in the policy and each VPC that's within scope of the policy, using the association priority settings that you specify in the Firewall Manager policy.

claim: Firewall Manager has three mandatory prerequisites (AWS Organizations with all features, a Firewall Manager administrator account, and AWS Config enabled on member accounts) and one optional prerequisite (AWS Resource Access Manager sharing, for Network Firewall and DNS Firewall policies).

Enable AWS Config on accounts - Enable AWS Config for each member account in your organization.
